A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the relocated proof of Lemma 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, CIFAR-10 likelihood experiments, and image-generation, blurring, and compression analyses on higher-resolution datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds likelihood summaries in Table 2 and Stable Diffusion examples in Figures 12–13.

M1.justification: The augmented SDEs, mode-tracking procedure, Gaussian approximation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. HP-ODE becomes HD-ODE through terminology changes. Appendix M documents the existing CIFAR models rather than establishing a new architecture or training procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix O substantially extends coverage to text-conditioned latent image generation with Stable Diffusion v2.1, using train, cat, and forest-tent prompts. This introduces different conditioning inputs and a latent-space generation setting beyond v1's pixel-space image and toy-distribution evaluations. Existing datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds PF-ODE sampling as an explicit comparator against HD sampling on CIFAR-10, alongside reverse-SDE sampling. v1's direct CIFAR comparison in Figure 7 used random reverse-SDE denoising samples. The high-resolution 'Original' sampler identities are newly documented rather than demonstrably new comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix N adds an unconditional CIFAR likelihood comparison with 1,024 samples per strategy and PF-ODE scoring, except for explicitly starred estimator rows. The existing 512-sample estimation-bias experiment remains. The new Stable Diffusion evaluation uses thresholds 0.2T, 0.4T, and 0.6T and prompts prefixed with 'A photo of'.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends quantitative threshold sensitivity analysis to both CIFAR training objectives, while Figure 12 tests how threshold changes affect Stable Diffusion outputs. These supplement the retained Gaussian-mixture, blurring, compression-correlation, and high-resolution threshold analyses rather than replacing them.

E5.justification: Appendix N newly reports mean NLL plus or minus one standard deviation in Table 2. This adds explicit numerical dispersion summaries beyond v1's distribution plots. These describe variation across generated samples; neither version establishes repeated-training uncertainty or adds seed-based significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial numerical results across samplers, thresholds, and model variants. For example, CIFAR10-ML reports 4.17 bpd for PF-ODE, 4.44 for reverse-SDE, and 1.25 for HD at 0.5T. Stable Diffusion examples add qualitative findings. These extend the evidence; the original figures and reported correlations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Core theorem statements and proofs are retained, and Lemma 1's proof moves from Appendix K to L. New Appendix K derives computational cost estimates. Separately, Equation 31 loses the g(t) multiplier on its stochastic term, introducing a mathematical inconsistency with the unchanged Theorem 2.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds an explicit recommendation that high-density regions should also be avoided for high-quality image generation. The principal claims about likelihood tracking, mode tracking, and unrealistic high-density images remain; renaming the sampler does not change its claimed contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix P adds a substantive interpretation connecting likelihood, image simplicity, and local intrinsic dimension, although it supplies no direct LID measurements. Appendices K and R quantify computational obstacles and newly explain why inexpensive stochastic likelihood tracking need not beat PF-ODE in total cost. The linear-drift and smooth-mode restrictions were already documented in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix M substantially expands reproducibility information with the U-Net implementation and hyperparameters, score parameterization, noise scheduling, two million training steps, batch size 128, and EMA weight 0.99. v2 also documents sampler identities and previously unspecified sample counts. These disclosures do not establish that existing experiments were changed or rerun.

R1.justification: New references support latent diffusion, classifier-free guidance, local intrinsic dimension, and cartoon generation. Appendix Q explicitly distinguishes studying density landscapes from designing cartoon generators, discussing Zhao et al. and AnimeGAN. The existing likelihood-estimation and typicality positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes 'high-density' terminology, updates author and conference information, adds acknowledgments and appendix cross-references, and makes localized prose revisions. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact; the additional scientific appendices do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figures 12–13, updates figure labels and captions, and adjusts headers and author layout. Existing figures retain their substantive displays. Figure 8's caption changes PNG to JPG even though its axis and surrounding discussion still specify PNG.

improvement.justification: The added training details, likelihood summaries, Stable Diffusion examples, and computational qualifications make the paper easier to reproduce and assess. These strengthen an otherwise retained scientific contribution. The gains are moderated by the new missing g(t) factor in Equation 31, the PNG/JPG caption inconsistency, and the interpretive rather than directly measured LID explanation. Overall, the additions provide a limited net improvement.
